newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec existing home sales fell 3.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec existing home sales fell 3.5 pct.

text.p: Sales of existing U.S. homes fell 3.5 percent in December to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.87 million units from a revised 4.01 million units in November, the National Association of Realtors said Monday.
Wall Street economists had forecast December sales of 4.0 million units.
The December sales rate was the same as the rate of 3.87 million in December 1995.
For all of 1996, existing home sales rose to 4.086 million units from 3.802 million in 1995.

The full year 1996 result of 4.086 million existing homes sold was a record number that the realtors' group attributed to the economy's steady expansion without generating strong inflationary pressures and to mortgage rates that were low by historical standards.

"The soft landing of the economy and favorable interest rates contributed to affordable conditions in both the first-time buyer and move-up homebuyer markets," said John Tuccillo, chief economist for the group.
